title: Containment Days and the Containment Charge — Installation Jobs Lead-Safe Work
content:
**Containment days — lead-safe work on Installation Jobs**

Containment is set up afresh on every crew day of an **Installation Jobs** record worked under lead-safe practices. The containment days are whichever is larger of the crew days on the job's booking and the crew days already logged at the home, and they decide how the containment charge is worked out:

| Containment days | Containment charge |
|---|---|
| 3 or more | the method's lead-safe fee per opening multiplied by the openings on the job, never less than the method's minimum per job multiplied by the containment days |
| 2 | the method's lead-safe fee per opening multiplied by the openings on the job plus a $60.00 containment re-set, never less than the method's minimum per job |
| 1 | the method's lead-safe fee per opening multiplied by the openings on the job, never less than the method's minimum per job |

In the 2-day row the $60.00 re-set is added before the minimum is compared. In the 3-or-more row the floor is the minimum per job taken once for every containment day.

## Worked examples (hypothetical figures: 45.00 per opening, minimum 175.00)

| Openings on the job | Containment days | Working | Containment charge |
|---|---|---|---|
| 7 | 4 | 315.00 against 175.00 times 4, that is 700.00 | 700.00 |
| 20 | 3 | 900.00 against 525.00 | 900.00 |
| 3 | 2 | 135.00 plus 60.00 is 195.00, against 175.00 | 195.00 |
| 2 | 2 | 90.00 plus 60.00 is 150.00, against 175.00 | 175.00 |
| 5 | 1 | 225.00 against 175.00 | 225.00 |

## Counting containment days (hypothetical)

A job booked for 2 crew days on which 3 crew days have already been logged has 3 containment days; a job booked for 3 crew days with 1 logged has 3.
